PullRequest.Title: chat: label plugins and marketplaces managed by a GitHub Team
PullRequest.Body: ## Context A GitHub Team can assign plugins to its members and supply plugin marketplaces. The Copilot runtime already reports this: installed plugins and marketplaces carry a `team` flag. The Agent Host dropped that flag when it converted the runtime's inventory into its own types, so nothing in the UI could tell a Team plugin or marketplace apart from one the user added. ## What changes for the user Plugins and marketplaces that come from the user's GitHub Team are now labeled wherever they are listed. **Plugins list.** A "Managed by your GitHub Team" tag sits beside the plugin name, using the same shield icon and style as the existing "Managed by your organization" tag. The hover reads "Assigned by your GitHub Team. You can still enable or disable it." **Plugin detail page.** The same tag appears in the header. **Browse page.** The Team marketplace's section title carries the tag, and the source menu lists it as "name (Managed by GitHub Team)". **Manage Plugin Marketplaces quick pick.** The row description reads "Managed by GitHub Team", next to the existing "Default" and "Unavailable" descriptions. ## How it works - **Agent Host.** `IAgentPluginInstallation` and `IAgentPluginMarketplace` gain an optional `team` flag, filled from the runtime. Plugins published in session state carry a new `vscode.customizationTeam` metadata entry, following the pattern of the existing organization metadata. Hosts that don't report it simply show no label. - **Workbench.** The flag is carried on marketplace info, customization items, installed plugins, and Browse sources. - **UI.** One shared tag component and one rule, in `customizationTeamProvenance.ts`, serve every surface. Row accessible labels and the Browse accessible view include the label. ## Things reviewers should know - **Provenance, not a lock.** A Team-assigned plugin can still be enabled or disabled. When something is both Team provided and organization managed, only the organization label shows, because organization settings decide its state. - **Rows follow the session's activation.** A Team assignment turns a plugin on for the session without changing the user's global setting. A runtime-installed row now takes its enabled or disabled appearance from its session plugin, matching its switch, instead of from the global setting. - **Labels need a live session.** In my testing the runtime reported Team plugins and marketplaces only for a live Copilot session. Before the chat's session starts, the lists come from the global inventory, which had no Team information, so no label shows. The existing organization requirement for runtime-installed plugins behaves the same way. - **Remove is still offered for Team marketplaces.** The runtime documents that Team marketplaces are not persisted and cannot be removed, so that action is unlikely to succeed. I left it unchanged here; hiding it is a possible follow-up. - **Uninstalled plugins.** The runtime does not flag individual plugins while browsing a marketplace, so an uninstalled plugin is identified as Team provided only through its marketplace. ## How to test 1. Sign in with an account that belongs to a GitHub Team with assigned plugins or a Team marketplace. 2. Start a Copilot CLI chat and send a message, so the session is live. 3. Open Customizations and check **Plugins**, a Team plugin's detail page, and **Browse**. Open the source menu on Browse, then **Configure Marketplaces** for the quick pick. The screenshots above are from a local build following these steps. ## Validation - `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed. - `./scripts/test.sh` on the nine affected test files (Agent Host inventory and metadata, customization item provider, marketplace quick pick, marketplace workbench service, Plugins list, plugin detail, Browse page): passed. - `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: passed. - `node --experimental-strip-types build/hygiene.ts `: passed. - A new component fixture, `TeamProvidedAgentHostPlugins`, renders the tag with mock data and is not CI blocking. - Not covered by a unit test: the wiring that gives the plugin detail page the session's Team information. I verified it in the running build (second screenshot).

Scenarios.Scenario: Discover and publish plugin inventory when a Copilot session starts or customizations refresh.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing runtime inventory and discovery must settle before authoritative plugin state is published. The change attaches Team provenance to those existing results; it adds no await or discovery request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the global runtime plugin inventory and, when installed plugins and a live session exist, its effective inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One global inventory request and at most one live-session inventory request per invocation, serving all installed plugins.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same inventory requests already supplied installation ownership and effective enablement; the diff reads team from their existing results.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaited inventory work precedes the returned plugin list.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read repository enablement and parse/watch installed plugin content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing repository-setting read per applicable inventory invocation; parsing per uncached plugin resource and content revision, with watchers owned per resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same settings reads, parsing, and watcher ownership existed; provenance does not cause additional reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial parsing is awaited before runtime customizations are constructed. Warm content is reused.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read runtime plugins and obtain the existing supplemental session inventory for managed plugins without content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Collection-wide inventory requests per discovery, not one request per plugin.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical calls and iteration; changed lines only extend metadata on already-selected plugins.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing inventory requests precede constructing plugin customizations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Carry Team provenance in the existing customization state payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one small metadata property per published plugin per existing publication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Published the same plugin collection without the Team property.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds bounded payload and shallow-copy work to existing state construction and transport.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Installed plugins, plugin contributions, and distinct live discovery anchor sets. The added metadata is one optional boolean per plugin, not per contribution.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Runtime-plugin refreshes use the existing Sequencer; installed-plugin parsing uses Promise.all. Chats sharing an anchor set share discovery. None of these scheduling rules changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Parsed runtime content remains keyed by resource, version, and content revision, including settled unsuccessful parsing. Existing watchers invalidate content and are removed for disappeared resources. Team metadata does not change content revisions or parse-cache keys.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed hunks and surrounding inventory, parsing, cache, watcher, and publication code were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual inventory sizes and runtime latency are unknown. No increase in boundary-call cardinality or scheduling was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance regression: existing expensive work is unchanged and the added metadata cost is small and proportional to the existing inventory.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, search, scroll, and update the Plugins list.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing provider-item fetch and installed-item filtering precede tree updates. Team visibility and session-effective enabled state are then computed synchronously for rendered rows.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve runtime plugin inventory while obtaining provider customizations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One inventory request per distinct runtime provider per provider fetch, typically one provider, shared across its plugin rows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same grouped inventory fetch supplied activation and organization control. Team provenance is extracted from that inventory without further requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Already awaited before provider items are returned; searches can reuse the item-source promise.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Session plugin count S and rendered installed rows V. New row computations perform several O(S) in-memory lookups per row; the prior organization/action pairing already scanned the same session collection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider-item promises are shared by the item source. Rendering is synchronous and virtualized; row autoruns are replaced on rerender and disposed with templates.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: PureItemProviderItemSource caches the unfiltered provider promise, invalidates on provider changes, and clears failed promises. The new observable stores the current session plugin array rather than accumulating historical arrays or keys.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: provider caching, collection lookup callers, row virtualization, and disposal paths were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Plugin and viewport sizes vary. Additional local scans and a few badge nodes/listeners per virtualized template do not establish significant jank at realistic inventory sizes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Added computations and nodes are bounded by current data/templates, with no new per-row IPC, filesystem work, or leaked subscriptions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an installed plugin detail page and receive live provenance changes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening the page starts the existing README load. The new provenance callback reads current in-memory session/plugin state; later Team changes update installed state and the tag without rerunning README or contribution loading.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the selected installed plugin's README through IFileService, potentially across a remote filesystem provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One README read per existing full detail render; Team-only updates use updateInstalledState instead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same full renders loaded the same README. The new observable dependency does not invoke renderReadme on a provenance-only update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: README content appears asynchronously; Team-tag computation adds no wait before reading or displaying it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected plugin, its README size, and the session plugin collection searched by the provenance callback.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single replaceable input-state autorun observes the selected item. Existing asynchronous README results are guarded by render generation and item identity.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new content cache or remote lookup is introduced. Session items are reused from the list; input autoruns and the detail-owned tag/hover are disposed through existing lifecycle stores.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: setInput, its autorun branches, renderItem, updateInstalledState, and loadPluginReadme were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: README sizes and filesystem latency are unknown but do not change the causal conclusion. Additional local lookup cost depends on session inventory size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance regression: provenance changes remain an in-memory header/state update, not repeated content I/O.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browse marketplace shelves, choose sources, and read the accessible Browse view.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing source discovery and catalog/preview requests populate Browse. The diff carries Team provenance into source sections, menu labels, accessible text, and a disposable section-header badge.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List provider marketplaces and browse the chosen marketplace through the agent-host service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One inventory request per existing refresh; one browse request per queried provider-marketplace page, returning its plugin collection before existing local filtering/paging. Shelf previews are per distinct source, not per displayed plugin.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same list and browse operations already populated the same shelves and menu sources. The diff adds a label-sensitive equality check, not an item-level request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing requests gate source/catalog results. A provenance transition may refresh affected source results through the pre-existing invalidation mechanism.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Delegate existing marketplace inventory/browse and other catalog-provider queries to runtime or provider services.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing source/page-level calls, with runtime-internal network behavior outside the inspected code. No new per-plugin network fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider operations were already on the Browse path; new flags do not change query size or page iteration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing provider latency affects catalog readiness; badge rendering itself is local.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct enabled marketplace sources M and their paged resources. Badges scale with visible source sections, not every marketplace entry.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Source-shelf previews are requested sequentially in loadSourceSections. Aggregate catalog queries use existing parallel provider queries. No concurrency policy changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing page-level browse catalog caching remains. Platform initial-page caches are keyed by provider, media type, and page size, expire after ten minutes, and provide cached progress while queries revalidate. Provider source identity comparison now notices a Team-label transition and uses the existing source-change invalidation path; unrelated changes still compare equal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for source/page cardinality, sequential previews, cache behavior, and disposal; runtime-internal transport costs are not visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Marketplace counts and provider latency are unknown. The additional refresh is tied to an actual provenance-label transition, not every provider event.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance bug. Existing boundaries retain their cardinality, and source-header tags are disposed before Browse reconstruction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Manage Plugin Marketplaces and display marketplace descriptions.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing provider inventory list resolves before constructing the quick pick. The added description is computed locally from each returned marketplace.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call provider.list(sessionResource), which forwards to agent-host marketplace inventory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One collection-wide list per existing picker-loop iteration, not one request per marketplace row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical list call and iteration; only the returned row-description text changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing list request gates picker display.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configured provider marketplaces M; one additional conditional description per row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The management loop awaits one inventory list before each quick-pick presentation. No new tasks are scheduled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is introduced; inventory is listed through the same provider path each time the existing management loop presents the picker.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: quick-pick construction and its provider/runtime forwarding path were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Marketplace count and inventory latency are unknown; neither request count nor critical-path scheduling changes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; the change is local label formatting over an already-fetched collection.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete 29-file inventory and every diff page, then traced performance-sensitive inventory, metadata publication, reactive list/detail rendering, Browse queries/cache invalidation, and quick-pick paths. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue or concrete performance-regression fix was found. No new subprocess or database work was identified.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
